summary: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kunga Chöphel, Zimwok Rinpoche, Geshe Tsechok in 1929, and the 13th Dalai Lama until around 1933. In 1928, he became Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche studied under numerous masters including Kalu Rinpoche (1959), Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (until ~1981), Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (until ~1991), and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (until ~1996). He founded Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chong Go is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Dongguk University and trained under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim until circa 2012.

Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney (~2011–2015) under Mark Allon, Rupert Gethin, D. Christian Lammerts, and Claudio Cicuzza, becoming an honorary associate there around 2016.

Christian Bernert is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna (2000–2009) under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Ngawang Jorden, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, Gerald Hödl, and Sherab Gyaltsen Amipa.

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University (~1999–2004) under John Powers, Sibajiban Bhattacharyya, and others. He held a fellowship at the Asiatic Society and joined the College of Charleston (~2006).
Christian Gottlob Heyne worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1748–1752) and held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1812.

Christian Haskett specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Advised by Robert A. F. Thurman and others, he earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~2003–2010) and held a post at Washington and Lee University around 2014.
Christian Hermann Weisse was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig University (~1818–1822). He later served on the faculty at Leipzig University from circa 1828 to 1866.
Christian Jochim specializes in religious studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Southern California by 1980 and served as a professor at San Jose State University.

Christian K. Wedemeyer specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University (~1993–1999) under Robert A. F. Thurman. His appointments include Columbia University, University of Copenhagen (~2000–2003), and University of Chicago (~2003–present).

Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen worked in linguistics, religious studies, history, and archaeology. He pursued his education at the University of Marburg (~1808–1809) and the University of Göttingen (~1809–1813).

Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bergen Cathedral School, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn (~1822–1827) under August Wilhelm Schlegel. He served as außerordentlicher Professor at the University of Bonn from 1830 to 1876.

Christian Lee Novetzke focuses on Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard Divinity School, Harvard University, and Columbia University. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~2002–2006) and the University of Washington (~2006–present).
Christian Lindtner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his filosofiske doktorgrad at the University of Copenhagen (~1971–1982), where he also held a professorship in 1982.

Christian Luczanits specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology, earning a Magister at the University of Vienna (~1986–1998). He held posts at Vienna, Lumbini International Research Institute, UC Berkeley, Stanford, and the Rubin Museum of Art (~2010–2014).

Christian Matthias Boehm works in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (~2001–2005) under John T. Carpenter, also studying under Toshifumi Konno.
Christian Wittern specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He held a position at Hanazono University from circa 1996 to 2001 and became a professor at Kyoto University around 2004.
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1986–1991). Around 2009, she became a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3.

Christine Mollier specializes in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She served as Director of Research at the CNRS (1989–1995) and as Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago (2002).
